item.title: Norman Jones parts ways with Social Circle after three seasons
item.description: Head coach of the Social Circle Redskins boys basketball program Norman Jones is leaving the team after three seasons. Social Circle City Schools (SCCS) posted a job opening for a “Head Basketball Coach” on Tuesday, though it was not clear at the time which coaching job was open. SCCS Communications and Media Manager Kari Willis confirmed to The Covington News on Thursday that the school had “mutually agreed to part ways” with Jones.

item.title: Suspect charged in Thanksgiving vehicular homicide
item.description: A suspect in a Thanksgiving crash that killed a pregnant woman and her unborn child was booked in the Newton County Detention Center on Monday.

item.title: City council decides against implementing ordinance to decriminalize minor marijuana possession
item.description: The Covington City Council voted against adopting an ordinance decriminalizing possession of one ounce or less of marijuana at their March 2 meeting. With the council voting 2-4, the motion to adopt the change failed to pass, and no new action has been put into place.

item.title: Alcovy Lady Tigers continue strong stretch; Newton boys pick up first win of season
item.description: The Alcovy Tigers and Newton Rams split matchups on the soccer pitch this Tuesday as the two rivals battled it out at Sharp Stadium. The girls matchup saw Tigers’ striker Zariah Strozier at her best as the South Carolina State signee scored a hat trick in a 3-1 victory. On the boys side, the Rams broke out of their five-game skid with a 6-0 victory.

item.title: Marcello Banes, Stephanie Lindsey federal trial pushed back for second time
item.description: For the second time, the federal criminal trial against suspended Newton County Chair Marcello Banes and District 3 Commissioner Stephanie Lindsey has been pushed back.

item.title: Two candidates qualify for District 5 Board of Education seat
item.description: Two challengers will vie for the open District 5 Board of Education seat this November.

item.title: Democratic showdown set between incumbents, challengers in primary race
item.description: Both the District 2 and District 4 seats on the Newton County Board of Commissioners will be up for grabs in the Democratic primary.

item.title: Keisha Lance Bottoms visits Covington during her gubernatorial campaign
item.description: Keisha Lance Bottoms is looking to do something that no Democrat has done since 2003: Become the Governor of Georgia. The former Atlanta city councilwoman and mayor visited Covington on Feb. 28 to be the keynote speaker at the “Blue Affair Breakfast Fundraiser” hosted by the Newton County Democratic Party. There, Bottoms shared her priorities and answered questions from constituents within her party.

item.title: Newton County Schools to celebrate School Board Appreciation Week March 9–13
item.description: From March 9–13, Newton County Schools will join districts across Georgia in celebrating School Board Appreciation Week.

item.title: Commissioners extend moratoriums on data centers, convenience stores
item.description: The Newton County Board of Commissioners voted unanimously on Tuesday to extend the enacted moratoriums for data center and convenience store applications. The 30-day moratoriums were initially set to expire on March 18 and have now been extended through April 8.
